children: Shares of Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone fell 1.23% on Friday amid report of company submitting a binding offer of $3.3 billion (euro 3 billion) to acquire pan-European liquid storage and terminals operator Evos Terminals.
The stock was trading at Rs 1,848.90 on the NSE, down Rs 23.10, as of 9:58 am.

The Gautam Adani-led company is seeking to strengthen its presence in the global liquid storage and terminals sector, particularly in Europe, amid geopolitical volatility and growing concerns over energy security, The Economic Times reported, citing people familiar with the development.

Evos, owned by Igneo Infrastructure Partners, operates eight tank terminals with a combined storage capacity of 6.4 million cubic metres across seven ports in five European countries. Its EBITDA was estimated at 200 million euros in 2025.

APSEZ submitted the binding offer earlier this week as part of a competitive auction process that has attracted interest from global investors and operators, including KKR, EQT, Macquarie, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, BlackRock and CPP Investments. A final decision is expected in the coming weeks, ET reported.

The overseas expansion push comes after Adani Ports lost its bid for UK-based Associated British Ports to superannuation fund IFM last week. On Wednesday, the company's management said it was evaluating 20 assets, including ports and terminals, as part of its global expansion plans.

title: Adani Ports places $3.3 billion bid for Evos Terminals; stock falls 1%
